invariant: A release rollback is a DECLARED, executable, evidence-preserving procedure: the trigger conditions, the human authorisation, the exact package identity rolled back TO, the in-flight-run package-pinning rule and the evidence that must survive are all declared here; every release-affecting event is an append-only hash-chained release-journal record; and a rollback target that is not attestable is refused rather than assumed.

scope.portable_tier: This repository and the artefacts it produces: a compiled package, its complete-package inventory, its deterministic archive, its external release-package attestation, the release journal and the preserved evidence. Everything in this policy marked portable is satisfiable here with no installed host.
scope.installed_host_tier: Anything that MUTATES what a live Rogo install resolves to — writing the versioned install destination, writing or re-pointing the active pointer, promotion and rollback transactions, and post-rollback installed behaviour parity. PERMANENTLY EXCLUDED from the portable programme, not deferred. Read-only verification of an already installed package's installation receipt, active-pointer bytes, promotion receipt and rollback identity is permitted and is mandatory before runtime may derive PRODUCTION_ACTIVE; that verification does not mutate the host and is not portable evidence that a promotion transaction was performed. The EXCLUDED_INSTALLED_HOST clauses below remain declared exclusions for mutation and live-transaction proof, never waivers.

trigger_conditions.title: What may trigger a release rollback
trigger_conditions.statement: A rollback may be opened only by one of the declared trigger conditions below, each of which names the mechanism that detects it. A condition not on this list is not a rollback trigger; it is either a new declared trigger (policy_version bump) or an ordinary defect to be fixed forward. No trigger executes a rollback by itself.
procedure_steps: Name the trigger_id that fired and capture the detecting mechanism's own output as the trigger finding.
Write the trigger finding to the rollback evidence directory before anything else happens; it is the reason the rollback exists and is preserved forever.
If the observed condition matches no declared trigger_id, STOP: either fix forward, or add the trigger here and bump policy_version — never roll back on an undeclared trigger.
evidence: the detecting mechanism's own output (attestation verification findings, closure mismatch error, failing gate receipt)

triggers.detected_by: scripts/lib/release_certification.mjs validateReleaseCertificationEvidence — a hash-bound evidence class no longer verifies against the promoted package.
scripts/lib/release_package_attestation.mjs verifyReleasePackageAttestation — the promoted package's inventory, archive or sealed product identity has diverged from its external attestation.
the release tag's bound source commit and tree no longer match the package the tag names; the tag's certification is invalidated by construction.
scripts/lib/source_identity.mjs checkActiveRuntimeCodeClosure — the live runtime-code closure is not the closure the promoted package identity declares, so runs refuse to start.
a registered delivery or validation gate that was green on the previous known-good package and is red on the promoted one, with both results bound to their package identities.
a vendored runtime dependency in the promoted package's closure must be removed or replaced for licence or supply-chain reasons, so the promoted closure may no longer be distributed.
an explicit written instruction from the release owner naming the package identity to withdraw and the retained target to return to.

authorisation.title: Who may authorise a rollback, and where it is recorded
authorisation.statement: Only the human release owner authorises a rollback. Automation may detect a trigger, assemble evidence and write the journal record, but it may never decide that a rollback happens. The authorisation must exist as a durable record before the rollback journal record is written, and the journal record must cite it.
procedure_steps: The release owner records the decision: the trigger_id, the package identity being withdrawn and the retained target identity being returned to.
Open a work-package issue card for the rollback under programme/ and reference it from the journal record's rollback.authorisation_reference.
Only then run the rollback procedure; a rollback journal record whose actor.kind is "automation" is refused by the validator.
evidence: the rollback journal record's actor and rollback.authorisation_reference fields

record_required: programme issue card naming the trigger, the withdrawn identity and the target identity
release-journal rollback record with actor.kind = human and a non-empty authorisation_reference

rollback_target_identity.title: Which package identity you roll back TO
rollback_target_identity.statement: A rollback target is one exact package identity expressed in product-identity/2.0 terms, not a branch, a version string or a nickname. The target must be attestable: verifyReleasePackageAttestation over the retained package bytes must PASS and the attestation must bind exactly the runtime-code closure being returned to. A target that cannot be attested is not a rollback target and the rollback is refused.
procedure_steps: Read the retained package's external release-package attestation (kept beside, never inside, the package bytes).

Run verifyRollbackTargetAttestation (scripts/lib/release_journal.mjs) over the retained package root, its attestation and its deterministic archive, passing the runtime-code closure digest you intend to return to.
Refuse the rollback outright if the verdict is not PASS: the retained bytes have moved, the archive does not match, or the attestation binds a different closure.
Carry the verified target identity into the journal record's rollback.to block in full: source commit, source tree, runtime-code closure, complete-package inventory, archive and attestation digests.
evidence: the retained package's external release-package attestation
the retained package's deterministic ustar archive
the rollback journal record's rollback.to identity block

binding.note: required_package_mode names the mode a PRODUCTION rollback target must carry. While v3.7.7 is portable-sealed development, a development-mode target is journalled honestly as such and the target-mode requirement is the standing rule the certified tier inherits — it is never silently relaxed to make a development package look production-eligible.

retained_previous_known_good.title: The retained previous-known-good package
retained_previous_known_good.statement: At least one previous known-good package is retained in full — archive, external attestation and release manifest — before any newer package is promoted. Retention is a precondition of promotion, not something arranged after a failure. Retention is journalled as a retain record, and the validator refuses a rollback whose target has no earlier retain record.
procedure_steps: Before promoting a package, confirm the outgoing package's archive and external attestation are retained outside the package directory and are readable.
Append a retain journal record carrying the retained package's full identity block, including its inventory, archive and attestation digests.
Never delete a retained package while it is the newest retained known-good; retire it only with a supersede record naming the retained package that replaces it.
If nothing is retained, promotion does not proceed: an unretained release has no rollback.

retained_artefacts: certification or portable-dossier verdict bound to that identity

in_flight_run_package_pinning.title: In-flight runs: the package-pinning rule
in_flight_run_package_pinning.statement: A run's package identity is resolved once, at run start, and is immutable for the life of that run. A release rollback NEVER re-points an in-flight run onto a different package: a run either continues on the package it was pinned to, or it is stopped and terminated with the already-registered CANCELLED.user_or_system_stop reason, which preserves its evidence and leaves it resumable from its own checkpoints. A half-rolled-back run — one whose inputs came from one closure and whose outputs came from another — is the single outcome this clause exists to make impossible.
procedure_steps: Enumerate the in-flight runs at the moment of rollback and record each one's pinned runtime-code closure.
Default: let each pinned run finish on its own package (pinned_continue). Its outputs stay attributable to the closure that produced them.

Stop a pinned run only when the trigger makes its output untrustworthy (a critical-severity trigger). Terminate it with CANCELLED.user_or_system_stop, which is checkpoint-required and evidence-preserving.
Record every in-flight run in the rollback journal record with its run_id, its disposition and, for a stopped run, that registered reason code. A run absent from the record is an undeclared run.
New runs started after the rollback record resolve to the rollback target; that resolution is portable here and route-level on an installed host (see active_pointer_repoint, which is excluded).
evidence: the rollback journal record's rollback.in_flight_runs array
each stopped run's terminal outcome artifact carrying CANCELLED.user_or_system_stop
each pinned run's run-start identity resolution recording its closure

binding.pinning_seam: scripts/lib/source_identity.mjs resolveActiveSourceIdentity — every run-start identity resolution flows through it and asserts the active closure against the declared package identity

stop_path.why: The registered code is already owner_layer run_controller, checkpoint_required, evidence_preserved and resumable_from_checkpoint — exactly the semantics a rollback-stopped run needs. Minting a rollback-specific terminal reason would add a second vocabulary for a state that already has one.

evidence_preservation.title: What must survive a rollback
evidence_preservation.statement: A rollback preserves evidence or it is not a rollback. Every class below is never-delete: the withdrawn package's own bytes and attestation, the retained target's bytes and attestation, the trigger finding, the release journal itself and the artefacts of every in-flight run at the moment of rollback. Nothing is deleted to make a rollback tidy; a superseded artefact is retired by a journal record, never by removal.
procedure_steps: Copy the withdrawn package's archive and external attestation into the rollback evidence directory before the withdrawal is recorded.
Confirm the retained target's archive and attestation are still readable and still verify; they are the other half of the record.
Leave every in-flight run directory in place, stopped or continuing; a stopped run keeps its checkpoints so it stays resumable.
Append the rollback journal record last, listing the preserved evidence paths. The journal is itself preserved evidence and is never rewritten or truncated.
evidence: rollback-evidence/<rollback-sequence>/ containing the withdrawn package archive, its attestation and the trigger finding
the retained target's archive and attestation
the in-flight run directories named in the rollback record

preserved_classes.reason: The withdrawn package is the subject of the rollback; without its bytes the rollback record cannot be independently checked.
The target must remain independently attestable after the rollback, not only at the moment of it.

artefacts: the detecting mechanism's output that opened the rollback
the failing gate or verification receipt bound to the withdrawn identity
preserved_classes.reason: The reason for a rollback is part of the release record; a rollback without its cause is folklore.
Append-only and hash-chained: deleting or rewriting any record breaks the chain and is refused by the validator rather than repaired.

artefacts: run directories of every run in flight at the rollback
the terminal outcome artifact of each stopped run
preserved_classes.reason: A user's run is their evidence. A release decision may stop a run; it may never destroy what the run had already proven.

release_journal_record.title: The append-only release journal
release_journal_record.statement: Every release-affecting event is one append-only record in the release journal: compile, attest, tag, retain, promote, rollback, supersede. Records are hash-chained — record_hash is the canonical digest of the record body with record_hash removed, previous_record_hash is the preceding record's record_hash, and the first record opens the chain with null. Sequences are contiguous from zero. The journal is only ever appended to; a record is never edited, reordered or removed, and a journal that does not validate cannot be appended to.
procedure_steps: Append one record per release-affecting event, at the time of the event, under the journal lock.
Carry the digest of this policy in every record, so a policy edit is visible on every record sealed after it.
Validate the whole journal before every append; refuse to append onto a chain that does not verify.
Never repair a journal by rewriting it. A mistaken record is corrected by a later record that says so.

chaining.record_hash: canonical sha256 of the record body with record_hash removed
chaining.sequence: contiguous integers from 0; a gap, a reorder or a fork is refused

binding.append_only_proof: Writes are O_APPEND + fsync under a directory lock, then byte-prefix-verified: if any earlier byte changed, the write is reported as a defect rather than accepted.

deployment_status_transitions.title: What the rollback deployment status means
deployment_status_transitions.statement: The "rollback" member of DEPLOYMENT_STATUSES is the status of the package being WITHDRAWN, and it is terminal for that package identity: a withdrawn identity is never promoted again, it is superseded by a new compile. The rollback target is not restamped by the rollback; it is recorded at the status it held when it was last known good. Making the target the live route again is a route change on an installed host and is excluded.
procedure_steps: Record the withdrawn package with deployment_status "rollback" in its rollback journal record; the validator refuses any other status there.
Record the rollback target at the status it already held; do not invent a new status for it.
Never write a later promote record for a closure that a rollback record has withdrawn — the validator refuses it. Fix forward with a new compile instead.
evidence: the validator's refusal of a post-rollback re-promotion

rollback_is_not_run_resume.title: Release rollback is not per-run resumability
rollback_is_not_run_resume.statement: Release rollback and per-run resumability are different mechanisms answering different questions. Per-run checkpoints answer "can THIS run continue from where it stopped". A release rollback answers "which package is the release". Resuming a run never changes which release is live, and rolling back a release never resumes a run. Neither may be presented as evidence for the other.
procedure_steps: When asked whether the product can roll back a release, read this policy and the release journal — never the per-run checkpoint receipts.
Never resume a run across a package-identity change: the run is pinned, and a resume onto different bytes is a half-rolled-back run.
Keep the two vocabularies apart in reports: a checkpoint receipt is per-run evidence, a journal record is per-release evidence.
evidence: scripts/lib/release_journal.mjs (release rollback and the release journal)

distinguished_from: scripts/lib/release_checkpoint_store.mjs ReleaseCheckpointStore — per-RUN resumability from that run's own artefacts
scripts/lib/flow_runtime.mjs stage receipts — per-RUN stage progress
binding.reason: Per-run checkpoints say nothing about which package is the release; they were repeatedly mistaken for rollback capability, which is why the distinction is a clause and not a comment.

active_pointer_repoint.title: Re-pointing the active route to the rollback target
active_pointer_repoint.statement: On an installed host, a rollback finishes by re-pointing the active route from the withdrawn package to the retained target and reading the pointer back from a fresh session. This programme has no installed host, so this leg is not performed and is not claimed.
active_pointer_repoint.exclusion_reason: Requires write access to a live Rogo install's versioned install destination and active pointer. The installed half of P8.6 is permanently excluded by standing directive; no script in this repository may mutate a live install, so this clause is unsatisfiable here by construction rather than merely unfinished.

installed_identity_readback.title: Fresh-session installed identity read-back after a rollback
installed_identity_readback.statement: On an installed host, the rollback target's identity is read back from a fresh session — installed package digest, active pointer and runtime-code closure — before the rollback transaction is considered complete. That post-rollback transaction proof is not performed here. This exclusion does not prohibit the runtime's non-mutating verification of already-present installation, pointer, promotion and rollback records before it derives PRODUCTION_ACTIVE.
installed_identity_readback.exclusion_reason: Requires a fresh installed-host transaction after a rollback. Portable verification stops at the retained package's own attestation and cannot assert that installed transaction occurred. Runtime read-only identity verification is permitted but is not reported as this clause passing.

post_rollback_installed_parity.title: Post-rollback installed behaviour parity
post_rollback_installed_parity.statement: On an installed host, a rollback is followed by an explicitly authorised installed behaviour parity run proving the target still delivers. Not performed here.
post_rollback_installed_parity.exclusion_reason: Requires an authorised fresh-session installed run and, for the workbook leg, native Excel and visual review — the same two evidence classes this programme records as permanent declared exclusions. The portable substitute is the registered portable gate set run against the target's own bytes, which is a different claim and is reported as such.
